title: Culture and identity
grammarTitle: Present simple and continuous; question forms
objectives: Talk about yourself, your family and your traditions
Use the present simple for habits and the present continuous for actions now
Ask and answer questions about identity and culture
before: Read the text in the Reading tab
Prepare your answer to speaking question 1
during: Discuss: what makes up your identity?
after: Complete the writing task and self-assessment

vocab.ex: Language is an important part of my identity.
vocab.use: Noun. Who you are, as a person or a group.

vocab.ex: She is proud of her cultural heritage.
vocab.use: Noun. Traditions and history passed down. Collocation: cultural heritage.

vocab.ex: Having lunch together on Fridays is a family tradition.
vocab.exAr: تناول الغداء معًا يوم الجمعة تقليد عائلي.

vocab.ex: I feel that I belong to this community.
vocab.exAr: أشعر أنني أنتمي إلى هذا المجتمع.
vocab.use: Phrasal verb. Not used in the continuous form.

vocab.ex: Our community organises a festival every year.
vocab.use: Noun. People who live in the same area or share a background.

vocab.ex: He is proud of his family's history.
vocab.use: Expression. Followed by a noun or a gerund.

grammarExplain:
Present simple is for habits, routines and facts: Yusuf speaks Arabic at home. Add -s for he, she and it. Use do/does in questions and negatives: Does she belong to a club? She doesn't belong to a club.

Present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) is for actions happening now or around now: The children are wearing traditional clothes today.

Question forms: question word + do/does + subject + verb: Where do your grandparents come from?

grammar.q: Yusuf ___ Arabic at home every day.
grammar.e: ‘Every day’ shows a habit, so we use the present simple. With ‘Yusuf’ (he), add -s: speaks.

grammar.q: Look! The children ___ traditional clothes for the festival.
grammar.e: ‘Look!’ shows something happening now, so we use the present continuous: are wearing.

grammar.q: Where ___ your grandparents come from? (do / does)
grammar.e: ‘Your grandparents’ is plural, so we use do.

grammar.q: She ___ (not / belong) to this club. Write the full answer.
grammar.e: Present simple negative with she: does not (doesn't) + base verb.

grammar.q: Error correction: which sentence is correct?
o: What do you do on Fridays?
What you are doing on Fridays?
grammar.e: Questions need do/does before the subject: What do you do…? The verb stays in its base form.

reading: My name is Amina and I live in Birmingham. My parents come from Morocco, so I speak Arabic at home and English at school. Every Friday, my family has lunch together, and my grandmother tells us stories about her village. I am proud of my heritage, but I also feel British. For me, identity is not one thing. It is a mixture of language, family, traditions and the place where you live. At the moment, I am studying history at university, and I am learning about how people describe their own culture.

readingEx.q: Main idea: what is the text mainly about?
o: How language, family and place form identity
readingEx.e: The text says identity is a mixture of language, family, traditions and place.

readingEx.q: True or false: Amina speaks only English at home.
readingEx.e: False. She speaks Arabic at home and English at school.

readingEx.q: Specific information: when does Amina's family have lunch together?
readingEx.e: The text says: ‘Every Friday, my family has lunch together.’

readingEx.q: Vocabulary in context: ‘heritage’ is closest to…
readingEx.e: Here ‘heritage’ means the history and traditions that a family or culture passes down.

readingEx.q: Inference: how does Amina probably feel about her identity?
o: She is comfortable with more than one
She is ashamed of her heritage
readingEx.e: She is proud of her heritage and also feels British, so she accepts both.

script:
Sara: Hi, I'm Sara. Are you new here?
Omar: Yes, I'm Omar. I'm studying engineering.
Sara: Where are you from?
Omar: I'm from Leeds, but my family comes from Egypt. We speak Arabic at home.
Sara: That's interesting! Which traditions are important to your family?
Omar: Eating together on Fridays. What about you?

listenEx.q: True or false: Omar was born in Egypt.
listenEx.e: False. He is from Leeds; his family comes from Egypt.

listenEx.q: Omar's family eats together on ___. (one word)

speak: Introduce yourself. Where do you live, and what do you do every day?
Describe a tradition in your family. Why is it important to you?
Do you think language is part of identity? Give reasons.
write: Write 60–80 words about your identity. Include at least four vocabulary items, one present simple sentence and one present continuous sentence.
